status: Fixed in source; regression validator verified
area: Task-ledger governance integration fixture authority drift
finding: The stale-framework-lock fixture created only a generic scope lock after framework temporary claims began requiring an active task-direction lock. A separate historical-close fixture inherited a lane-bound claim while asserting pre-capability historical-delivery behavior. Both tests therefore failed before reaching the rule they were intended to verify.
expectedBehavior: Integration fixtures must model every authority prerequisite of the public seam they exercise, while deliberately testing legacy or unbound behavior only when that state is explicit. Production claim and lane-capability gates remain fail-closed and are not weakened to accommodate fixtures.
evidenceOrRepro: Before the repair, node --strip-types scripts/validate-task-ledger-governance.ts --mode validate failed first with ATM_FRAMEWORK_TEMP_CLAIM_TASK_BINDING_INVALID for TASK-STALE-DEMO-0002, then with ATM_LANE_BORROWED_ACTOR_BLOCKED for TASK-CLOSE-ORCH-0005. After the fixture declares the required direction lock and explicitly removes lane binding for the legacy close case, the same command passed on 2026-08-14 in 69.5 seconds; npm run typecheck also passed.
followUp: Keep the fixture authority model adjacent to the assertion and retain this validator in the task-ledger governance family. When adding a new authority gate, search isolated integration fixtures for implied preconditions rather than weakening the gate or accepting an unrelated failure code.
